comments.body: u/jaykrown this post needs more detail on how you used AI in development. Saying you used AI isn't the same as explaining how. Rule 4 asks promotional posts to contribute by talking about the process. We're trying to keep "check out my game" posts from taking over the sub. If you don't update, this may be removed.

comments.author: jaykrown
comments.body:
# How we build

Rust. Physics, input, and race rules live in one shared crate — not copied into the client “for speed.” One name for a mass: body, static or moving, pull or push. Recoverable failures are typed errors. The sim and net path do not panic on a missing slot. No `unsafe`. Clippy denies the shortcuts. Tests cover the maps, the tape, and the board.

Live is the `main` branch on slingshotspeeders.com. New work lands on `test` first. A promote to production is deliberate. We do not hot-edit live.

# Who decides

Development is AI-assisted — Claude Opus 5 and Grok 4.6. Planning, architecture, decisions, coding standards, and the orbital mechanics knowledge come from James Masland.

Ship cosmetics are AI-assisted. James drew them and thought them up, then used AI to push the quality. He is a solo developer; that is the only way to ship this look this fast. AI is an assistant, never a full replacement, and will not be allowed to cheapen the art.
